summary: Polish/launch-readiness pass. Ran the existing 12 pytest backend tests (all pass) and full frontend regression: homepage calc (1960-04-15 standard -> Wednesday, July 15, 2026), SSI holiday shift (Aug 1 2026 Sat -> Fri Jul 31 2026 confirmed; no Sat/Sun in schedule), pre-1997 rule, mobile @390x844, skip-to-content link, header dropdown, country pages, legal pages, shared footer, and UK NI 42 -> Wednesday. One clear MOBILE horizontal overflow bug found in the header and two minor code-quality issues.

ui_bugs.issue: On mobile viewport 390x844 the page has horizontal overflow (scrollWidth=408 vs clientWidth=390). Scanner attributes the overflow to [data-testid=header-country-nav-trigger] whose right edge is at 408px because the header row (brand block + trigger button) does not fit at 390px. The screenshot shows the trigger button clipped off the right side. Fix ideas: shrink brand on <sm (hide 'INFORMATIONAL AID' subline on xs, or truncate CheckPayDate.com), or use a compact icon-only trigger on mobile with 'sr-only' text, or wrap header contents / reduce horizontal padding.

issues: React logs: 'Invalid DOM property fetchpriority. Did you mean fetchPriority?'. In App.js the hero attribute should be JSX-cased `fetchPriority="high"` (not `fetchpriority`). Doesn't break functionality but pollutes console and skips the intended priority hint.

The benefit-type <select> element has no id and therefore no associated <label htmlFor=...>. There is visible surrounding text ('1. Select Your Benefit Type') but assistive tech does not receive a programmatic label. Fix: add id to <select> and htmlFor on the label (the date input already does this correctly with id='birth-date').

action_items: Fix mobile horizontal overflow at 390px: shrink/hide the header brand subline or convert the header dropdown trigger to a compact icon+chevron on <sm so header fits without a horizontal scrollbar.
Change JSX attribute `fetchpriority` -> `fetchPriority` on the eager hero in App.js to silence the React warning and actually apply the fetch priority hint.
Add an id to the benefit-type <select> and use <label htmlFor='...'> so the visible label is programmatically associated (screen-reader a11y).
critical_code_review_comments: SiteFooter.jsx footer testids (footer-privacy-link, footer-terms-link, footer-contact-link, site-footer) all render on homepage, country pages and legal pages — good.

sitemap.xml is well-formed and lists 9 URLs (homepage + 5 country + 3 legal). robots.txt Cloudflare prepends managed content but the required lines 'User-agent: *', 'Allow: /' and 'Sitemap: https://checkpaydate.com/sitemap.xml' are all present at the end.
index.html has both JSON-LD blocks (@type: WebApplication, FAQPage) as required, plus title/description/canonical/og:/twitter: meta.
SSI schedule correctly avoids all weekend day_names; confirmed Aug 1, 2026 (Sat) -> Fri Jul 31, 2026 shift renders as the 'Next Payment' row. Pre-1997 schedule is on the 3rd (or prior business day).
App.js still ~1000 lines — carry-over recommendation from prior iterations: split Calculator/ResultCard/ScheduleTable/Header into smaller components for maintainability.
Consider giving the benefit-type <select> an id so its label can be linked with htmlFor (a11y).

success_rate.frontend: ~90% — all functional flows pass; 1 mobile layout bug, 1 console warning, 1 minor a11y label association

context_for_next_testing_agent: Container date is early July 2026. Standard 1960-04-15 -> Wednesday, July 15, 2026. SSI -> Friday, July 31, 2026 (shifted from Sat Aug 1). Pre-1997 -> Monday, Aug 03, 2026. The benefit-type control is a NATIVE <select> (not Radix), so use `page.locator('select').first.select_option('ssi'|'pre_1997'|'standard')`. When SSI/pre_1997 is chosen the birth-date input is hidden. Header dropdown trigger has data-testid=header-country-nav-trigger; items follow header-country-nav-<key>. Skip link is [data-testid=skip-to-content-link] with href=#main-content and receives the very first Tab focus. JSON-LD blocks are exactly 2 with @type WebApplication and FAQPage. Country page routes have trailing slashes.
rca of the issue: Mobile header overflow (390px): the header uses a single row containing a brand block (icon + 'CheckPayDate.com' + 'INFORMATIONAL AID' subline) on the left and a full-width 'Payment Date Checkers' Radix trigger button on the right. At 390px the combined intrinsic width (~408px) exceeds the viewport, so the trigger button's right edge is clipped and the page gets a horizontal scrollbar. The button DOM text is 'Payment Date CheckersCountries' — indicating the desktop and mobile labels are both in the DOM (one hidden with Tailwind hidden md:inline classes) but the outer button width is still driven by the visible short label + icon padding at 162px, and combined with the brand block padding it exceeds 390. Recommended fix: hide the 'INFORMATIONAL AID' subline on <sm (e.g., add hidden sm:block) OR reduce the trigger to just a globe icon + chevron on <sm, keeping the sr-only accessible text. Backend and every other flow are unaffected.
